outcome: An operator watching a run sees what each worker is doing turn by turn while it happens, on every lane, in an activity pane on the browser board and an activity screen in the TUI, fed from the journaled worker turns and tool results and pushed live over a content-bearing server-sent-event route when the serve host is driving the run.

acceptance.text: The cockpit projector gains one activity projection over the journaled worker-turn and tool-result events: for a run, optionally narrowed to a track, slice or dispatch, it returns an ordered, paged list of turns, each with its identity (slice, role, responsibility, attempt, try, turn), the bounded decoded parts of the worker turn and the tool results keyed to that turn, with omitted and redacted byte counts and dropped-event counts shown rather than hidden. It reads only what S1 and the existing tool-result observation journaled; it adds no second source of worker content and performs no new redaction of its own because none is needed. The existing metadata-only evidence projection and its page type are unchanged. Anchor: internal/cockpit/projector_test.go.

The serve host exposes the activity projection on a new route under the run's API, as a JSON page and, when the client accepts text/event-stream, as server-sent events whose frames carry the turn content. The stream resumes exactly from Last-Event-ID or an after offset with no gap and no duplicate, keeps the existing keepalive cadence, and shares the existing concurrent-stream gate and its SSE_LIMIT refusal. The existing events route keeps its contract byte for byte: invalidate frames that carry only the schema version and the through offset. The new route sits behind the same canonicalisation, origin, loopback and bearer rules as every other run route. Anchor: internal/cockpit/server_test.go.

When the serve host is the process driving the run, a bounded in-memory ring per live dispatch receives each turn projection from the observation hook at the moment it is emitted, and the stream route serves from the ring ahead of the journal so a watcher sees a turn without waiting for a poll. The ring is bounded in turns and bytes by declared constants, is dropped when the dispatch ends, is never persisted, and holds only projections that were already bounded and redacted for journaling. When the run is driven by another process the route serves the same content from the journal alone and says nothing false about liveness. A ring that is full drops its oldest turn and counts the drop; it never blocks the dispatch. Anchor: internal/cockpit/server_test.go and internal/runtime/tool_result_observation_test.go.

The browser board shows an activity pane for the selected work: the live dispatch's turns in order, each with the role, the turn number, the worker's bounded text, the tools it called and each tool result's pass or fail state and size, following new turns as they arrive and marking omitted and redacted content plainly. It opens the new stream only while the pane is visible and closes it when the pane or run changes. The embedded assets stay pinned and the static user-interface contract test is updated, not bypassed. Anchor: internal/cockpit/server_test.go and internal/cockpit/web_validator_test.go.

The TUI gains an activity screen reached from the board for the selected work, fed through the existing backend boundary from the same activity projection over the journal, refreshed on the existing refresh cadence, guarded by the same generation check that protects the other asynchronous loads, scrollable, and honest about narrow terminals. The TUI does not connect to the serve host; it stays a direct journal reader. The help overlay names the key. Anchor: internal/tui/model_test.go and cmd/sworn/tui_backend_test.go.

In a built-product journey with a scripted worker that takes several tool-calling turns, the activity route returns those turns in order while the dispatch is still running, the stream delivers a later turn to an already-connected client without a reconnect, and after the run completes the journal-backed page returns the same turns the live stream delivered. Anchor: test/e2e/surface_parity_linux_test.go and cmd/sworn/tui_pty_linux_test.go.

docs/run.md documents the activity pane and screen, the new route and its stream semantics, what is and is not retained, and the difference between a run the serve host drives and one it only observes. Anchor: docs/run.md.

constraints: One projection, two transports. The JSON page, the event stream, the browser pane and the TUI screen all render the activity projection of A1. The ring only shortens latency for the same projections; a surface never shows worker content that the journal will not also hold once the turn is journaled.

The activity surface is a view. It adds no command, no control, no authority and no second scheduler. Nothing a worker says in a turn is treated as a status, a verdict, a check result or a reason to act; park causes, refusals and receipts remain the only typed facts a seat decides from.

No token-level deltas in this release. --include-partial-messages is not added to any native argv and HTTP-lane streaming deltas are not routed into the ring. Granularity is the turn. The deferral is deliberate: deltas multiply stream bytes against the manifest-governed output budget and need their own accounting decision. The plan records it as a follow-up.

The serve host's HTTP posture is unchanged: hand-rolled routing in internal/cockpit/server.go, canonical paths, origin and fetch-site checks, loopback or TLS with bearer, bounded JSON admission. The new route is read-only and takes no body.

Content reaches a surface only in its bounded, redacted, journaled form. The activity projection decodes the head and tail spans for display and never reassembles, guesses or fetches omitted bytes. Terminal control sequences in worker content are neutralised before the TUI renders them, and the browser pane inserts content as text, never as markup.

The product MCP surface is not extended here. A seat-facing read of worker turns belongs with the typed explain read that follows this release; do not add an MCP tool for it in this slice. Shape the activity projection so that read can reuse it.
Telemetry export is unchanged: the new events are not exported to OpenTelemetry in this release.

Every listed check is a host check: contained implementers and verifiers consume engine-bound host evidence and never attempt nested containment or claim to have executed these commands. Each long process suite runs once per candidate in the phase order the engine defines.

This release changes no roster, model selection, budget, timeout, retry cap or fallback behaviour. The broad supporting package scope admits only this promised mechanism and its affected regression fixtures, adapters and documentation.

Known contained-workspace facts, not defects of this slice: cmd/sworn's TestTUIActionDriveSurvivesActionReturn fails in the sandbox with CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE and prints roughly 90 KB of DEBUG output; it passes on the host. Do not chase it and do not run it in the workspace. The PTY suites need a terminal the sandbox may not provide; rely on host evidence for them. internal/runtime exceeds Go's implicit 10-minute package deadline in the sandbox; pass -timeout=20m on your own package runs. The sandbox shell is dash without `which`. Never build a binary into the workspace root: an out-of-scope file at the root makes checkpoint capture refuse with CHECKPOINT_SCOPE_VIOLATION and fences the workspace; build into a temporary directory.

internal/protocol is the embedded protocol package. This slice needs no change to its receipt vocabulary, operation assets or pinned digests; if a design appears to need one, report it rather than re-pinning the bundle.
